statement: The 3x-1 verification floor, supplied and pushed, so J-negative-cycle-finance-is-the-juggler-mirror stops being a conditional table. THE FLOOR. Every 1 <= y < 2^44 = 17592186044416 reaches 1, 5 or 17 under g(y) = y/2 (y even), (3y-1)/2 (y odd) -- the shortcut 3x+1 map read on the negatives. Certificate: 112 chunks. The first 16, made with the plain descent walker verify_3x1.c, reach 2^40 (greatest step count 544 against a cap of 4000). The other 96, made 20 September 2026 on the laboratory machine with the archived sieve-plus-jump-table walker verify_3x1_jump.c, cover [2^40, 2^44) in chunks of 5*2^35 numbers: 8246337208320 odd starts counted exactly (walked plus sieved equals the width), 0 failures, 0 new cycles, greatest step count 704 against a cap of 40000 -- that walker counts sixteen steps per table jump and checks the drop only at a landing, so its counts overshoot by up to fifteen. Method: verify odd y ascending and stop when an iterate drops below y, which closes by induction once the chunks cover the interval and all passed; a return to y is checked against the three known cycles, and the step cap catches a cycle whose least element exceeds the start -- with the jump table a jump can carry past the return, so such a cycle surfaces as a STEPCAP, reported and never a silent pass. The sieve is unconditional on this side (neg_prefix_noncontracting: a contracting prefix drops every member of its class), and its class count at K = 24 is A076227(24) = 286581. Validated on the machine that ran it: with the 17-cycle removed from its known list the walker reports NEW CYCLE at 17, and it agrees with the plain walker on three already-verified windows; gcc 13.3 under WSL2, source digest, host and timings in runs.json, raw reports in p44_reports.log. A pure-Python reference iterating to a cycle element agrees with descent on every odd y < 300000. THE HOLE IN THE FIRST CERTIFICATE, FOUND AND CLOSED. The plain walker prints odd_starts = floor((limit - lo)/2) with lo odd, which undercounts each chunk by one; the committed total to 2^40 was short by 23, and the only launch value that reproduces the counts of chunks 1 to 7 is k*2^35 + 3. So the seven odd starts k*2^35 + 1, k = 1..7, lay between the chunks of the 2^38 certificate and were walked by nothing. Each reaches a known cycle by full iteration (118 to 232 steps to the first drop), as does every odd start within 64 of every legacy boundary; the probe now recovers every chunk's launch value from its record, lists every gap between chunks, verifies each, and the certificate is not clean otherwise. The floor statements at 2^38 and 2^40 were true; the certificates behind them were not tilings, and this row said 'tiling' twice. EXCURSIONS. The greatest landing value seen above 2^40, 121443575752945981388885320 (1.21e+26), exceeds the record 261160802435320822179964 from below 2^40, so the whole certificate's greatest known excursion is now 121443575752945981388885320. THE BOUND. Reading the kernel-checked neg_cycle_finance, 2(|x|-1)(3^o - 2^K) <= (K-o)3^o at a negative cycle's least |x|, at the floor 2^44: a fourth cycle of the 3x-1 shortcut map -- equivalently a fourth negative cycle of shortcut 3x+1, whose word is a Paper A CycleMin shape letter for letter by neg_cycle_word_is_juggler_shape -- has period at least 16483927, with 10400200 odd steps; the uniform and hug-word constants give the same length here. The history: 4404167 at 2^38, 9538065 (6017849 odd steps) at 2^40, 16483927 at 2^44; the 72448885240 of the conditional table needs 2^68. WHY IT IS THE JUGGLER'S BUSINESS. The negative cycles are the ones whose words the Juggler shares, and the inequality that consumes the floor is Juggler machinery. WHAT IT IS NOT. Not N_0, which stays 350000000 for the Juggler's own cycle floor; not a halt theorem for either map; not a Juggler cycle exclusion; no Juggler bound moves; Paper A's Remark 5.20 carries this floor, the bound 16483927 and the certificate's checksums since the revision of 20 September 2026 (Zenodo new version pending). The floor is empirical and is this laboratory's own computation -- the recorded search of OEIS, Roosendaal, Lagarias's bibliography and Chamberland section 6.1 found no published 3x-1 floor, which is not the same as none existing. Only the implication is kernel-checked. COST. [2^40, 2^44) took 27 minutes on 24 threads of the Ryzen 9 3900X, 9.9 core-hours at about 393 million odd starts per second per core; [2^44, 2^48) would be sixteen times that, an overnight run; 2^68 is a GPU project. SEARCH REPEATED 20 September 2026 from the laboratory machine with web access: still no published 3x-1 verification floor anywhere reachable -- both Lagarias bibliographies in full text, the whole local OEIS corpus, Wikipedia, Roosendaal, Ghosh, Tremblay, Cox -- and OEIS A037084's unattributed 'up to at least 100000000' (oeis-A037084) is the only statement found; the conditional table's shape is Sinisalo's 2003 Table 2 (J-negative-cycle-finance-is-the-juggler-mirror). The 2^44 floor is therefore the only one this laboratory can cite, and it is its own. REPRODUCED ON THE GPU, 21 September 2026: a CUDA implementation (verify_3x1_gpu.cu, the run identity g^a(y) - 1 = (3/2)^a (y - 1) for whole runs, the same mod-2^24 sieve, 128-bit state with an overflow report) agrees with the certificate on every quantity where the semantics coincide -- [3, 2^35) and [3, 2^40): max steps 508 and 544 and the peaks exact; [2^40, 2^44): 8246337208320 odd starts, no failure, no cycle, the landing peak 121443575752945981388885320 exact, max steps 703 exact against the jump walker's granular 704 -- in 26.2 s against the CPU's 1628 s on 24 threads (about sixty times; 26.1 s and 26.7 s on two runs); with the 17-cycle forgotten it reports NEW CYCLE at 17. At that rate 2^51 is about 1 hour from 2^44, 2^56 about 32 hours, 2^60 about 21 days. EXTENDED TO 2^51 ON THE GPU, 21 September 2026: the sweep of [2^44, 2^51) in 8 chunks, 59 minutes on the RTX 5090, 1117103813820416 odd starts (the exact count), no failure, no new cycle, no overflow, greatest step count 847, peak about 2^97.0; three 2^37 windows agree with the archived CPU jump walker under WSL (same walked and skipped counts, same peaks, the GPU's exact step counts below the CPU's granular ones by 72, 12, 48). The statement now reads: every 1 <= y < 2^51 reaches 1, 5 or 17, and the m-free period bound at that floor is 85137581 with 53715833 odd steps (16483927 at 2^44, unchanged, is Paper A's number). Records gpu_runs.json, gpu_chunks/, gpu_calibration/.
